bug_description.normalized: When Poppler renders the witness PDF, GfxCIDFont reads the attacker-controlled Type 0 font /Encoding object and sends its stream into CMap::parse2. parse2 allocates stack token buffers tok1/tok2/tok3 without initialization, then uses PSTokenizer::getToken to fill only the current token bytes plus a trailing NUL. On the witness path, the first parsed token in tok1 is shorter than the keyword "/WMode" and the second token is not "usecmap", so parse2 falls through to `strcmp(tok1, "/WMode")`. MemorySanitizer reports that this comparison reads uninitialized bytes from tok1's stack tail and crashes at poppler/CMap.cc:247.

source.description: First project-code statement on the vulnerable path that consumes the attacker-controlled /Encoding object from the PDF font dictionary and hands it to the CMap parser.
source.value_from: The witness PDF's Type 0 font dictionary provides an attacker-controlled /Encoding entry that resolves to a CMap stream; `obj1` is that object and is forwarded into CMap::parse.

tainted_value_origin.description: tok1 is a stack token buffer allocated without initialization. Only the bytes written by PSTokenizer::getToken and the trailing NUL become defined before strcmp reads it.

sink.description: MemorySanitizer crash site. strcmp reads tok1 while its stack tail is still uninitialized.
sink.note: The sanitizer trace reports uninitialized bytes in __interceptor_memcmp at offset 2 inside a 7-byte region and attributes the poisoned value to tok1's stack allocation in CMap::parse2.

root_cause.description: CMap::parse2 allocates the token buffers on the stack without zero-initialization even though later dispatch compares them against fixed string literals with strcmp after only partial token writes.
root_cause.note: The parser assumes tok1 contains a fully defined NUL-terminated token, but getToken only overwrites the current token prefix and one terminator byte. When a malformed CMap leaves tok1 shorter than "/WMode", the subsequent strcmp reaches untouched stack bytes.

parser_admitted.condition: The witness PDF's /Encoding object is a stream, so CMap::parse takes the stream branch and forwards obj->getStream() into the parse2 path instead of rejecting the encoding.

coarse_trace.summary: The harness loads the witness PDF and renders a page, which drives CID font encoding parsing inside Poppler.
The CID font loader retrieves the attacker-controlled /Encoding object from the font dictionary and invokes CMap::parse on it.
CMap parsing recognizes that the /Encoding object is a stream, resets that stream, and routes byte reads into CMap::parse2 through getCharFromStream.
parse2 tokenizes the CMap into uninitialized stack buffers; tok1 remains only partially defined and strcmp(tok1, "/WMode") consumes its uninitialized tail, producing the MSAN crash.

fine_trace.note: Consumes the attacker-controlled /Encoding object from the PDF font dictionary and starts CMap parsing for that object.

fine_trace.note: The attacker-controlled Encoding object is a stream, so the parser extracts its Stream* and dispatches to the stream-specific CMap parser.
Resets the attacker-controlled CMap stream and makes parse2 consume bytes from it via getCharFromStream.
Allocates the token buffers on the stack without initialization. MSAN later identifies tok1 from this stack frame as the origin of the poisoned bytes.
Reads the first attacker-controlled token from the CMap stream into tok1 before the main keyword-dispatch loop.
getToken defines only the token bytes it copied plus one terminating NUL. Any bytes in tok1 after index i remain whatever was already in the stack slot.
Reads the next attacker-controlled token into tok2 and enters the outer dispatch loop while preserving tok1 from the previous token.
On the witness path the second token is not `usecmap`, so control falls through and tok1 is left unchanged for the next keyword comparison.

MSAN sink. strcmp reads tok1 as a 7-byte `/WMode\0` comparison even though only a shorter token prefix and one NUL were written earlier; the sanitizer reports the first uninitialized byte at offset 2 of that read.

allocation_context.note: The sanitizer reports the uninitialized value as created by allocation of `tok1` in parse2; the concrete declaration is line 235.

format.name: PDF Type 0 font Encoding CMap stream
format.contract: The PDF must contain a Type 0 font whose /Encoding entry is a CMap stream parsed by CMap::parse2, and the witness stream must yield a first token shorter than `/WMode` followed by a second token that is not `usecmap`, so `strcmp(tok1, "/WMode")` reads tok1's uninitialized tail.
